newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called flat to up $5 ahead of US grind.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called flat to up $5 ahead of US grind.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called unchanged to $5 per tonne higher on Friday, as traders await the U.S. 1997 second quarter grind figures.
The U.S. grind data, slated for release this moring before the opening bell, are expected to rise some 5 to 10 percent compared with 1996 second quarter grindings, industry sources said.
But traders said only a sharply higher or lower reading would have an impact on prices.
In London, cocoa futures were weaker early Friday, but off lows. LIFFE September was down two stg at the midday break, to 1,022 stg, after ranging from 1,023 to 1,016 stg.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures fell sharply, pounded by chart-driven speculative selling. September tumbled $42 per tonne, to $1,534, after ranging from $1,560 to $1,526. Second-month December dropped $42, to $1,583, while the back months plunged $43.
Technically, dealers said September's next downside target was a gap on the charts between $1,525 and $1,516. Subsequent support was seen at $1,500.
